canonical_definition:
What it is. The available paper treats D4RL as Datasets for Deep Data-Driven Reinforcement Learning, described as a benchmark suite for offline reinforcement learning. In that usage, it appears specifically in risk-sensitive variants, with experiments run on four risk-sensitive D4RL tasks using public human preferences, as described in A Distributional Approach to Uncertainty-Aware Preference Alignment Using Offline Demonstrations.

What it is claimed to measure. The papers represented here do not report D4RL as measuring any construct or behavioral indicator, and no measured_by relationship is recorded for it.

Space of uses. Usage is illustrated in one paper as an experimental benchmark: the authors report that they "conduct experiments using public human preferences from Yuan et al. (2024) on four risk-sensitive D4RL tasks." No other measurement instrument is linked to it.
